issues.description: Regression suite was not executed (regressions_ran=0) and pov_before_reproduced=false, so no independent confirmation that legitimate copy behavior and other tests still pass beyond the two added unit tests.

getCanonicalFile() resolves symlinks inside the destination, which is a stronger stance than the official normalize-based fix; in rare setups where a legitimate symlinked subdir points outside dest, extraction could be rejected.

result.summary: Our patch fixes the CWE-022 tar-slip at the correct sink in Copy.java by canonicalizing both the destination and each entry path and rejecting any entry that does not resolve inside the destination directory (prefix terminated with File.separator to avoid sibling-prefix bypass). This is the CWE-022 defense of record and is semantically a superset of the official FilenameUtils.normalize() fix, additionally neutralizing symlink-based escapes. The main gap is verification coverage: no regressions were run and the POV did not reproduce pre-patch, though added unit tests confirm both rejection and legitimate extraction.
result.root_cause: Archive entry names read from the pod (entry.getName()) were passed unvalidated into new File(destination, name), allowing '../' sequences to write files outside the destination directory (tar slip / path traversal).
